findings.title: test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key, so its assertion fails
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe, the expected occurrence is built via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH), but the DetectorEvaluationResult it is compared against is produced by calling evaluate_group_key_value with group_key="group_key" (expected_result.group_key is passed in). build_mock_occurrence_and_event embeds handler.build_fingerprint(group_key) into the IssueOccurrence, so the expected occurrence has fingerprint ["<detector_id>:val1"] while the actual occurrence has ["<detector_id>:group_key"]. IssueOccurrence is a dataclass whose equality compares the fingerprint field, so the DetectorEvaluationResult equality check fails and this test errors on its first assert. The helper should be called with "group_key" (or the result built with "val1") so the fingerprints match.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated — it doesn't implement StatefulDetectorHandler's abstract methods
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from DetectorHandler (with a working stub evaluate returning []) to StatefulDetectorHandler with a bare `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook, so the class remains abstract and any instantiation raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler points at this class, and Detector.detector_handler does group_type.detector_handler(self); process_detectors only guards against a None handler, not an exception, so evaluating any Detector with type "metric_alert_fire" will now crash processing instead of returning no results as before. Either add stub implementations of the abstract methods or leave the handler non-abstract until the real implementation lands. (The TODO comment above the class — "This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction" — is also now stale, since it already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler.)

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate reads "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but this PR changed both the abstract DetectorHandler.evaluate signature and this implementation to return a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey (dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]). The stale docstring will mislead anyone implementing a new handler; it should describe the dict return.

findings.title: build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its `value` argument, so the value passed to the occurrence hook is never verified
findings.body: The test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event takes a `value` parameter but never uses it when constructing the IssueOccurrence/event_data. In test_state_results_multi_group the expected occurrence for "group_2" is built with value 6 even though the data packet sets "group_2" to 10, and the test still passes only because the helper discards the value. As written, no test would catch evaluate_group_key_value forwarding the wrong value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. Either include the value in the built occurrence (e.g., in evidence_data) so it is asserted, or at minimum pass the correct value (10) at this call site.
